Description.description: Unique identifier for Platform
The name the scope selector shows at platform scope.
A short code for reporting, such as IPA.
The person accountable for the platform. Not the Dataverse record owner.
Display order in the scope selector.
An inactive platform is hidden from the scope selector and kept for history.
A lab inside a platform. It holds teams, and the roll-ups at lab scope sum them.
Unique identifier for Lab
The platform the lab sits in. Every lab has one.
The person who leads the lab.
Unique identifier for Team
The lab the team sits in. Every team has one.
The person who leads the team.
Semicolon separated, the tools this team builds with. Matches the wp_productline labels.
A member of the team, and everything capacity needs to know about them.
Unique identifier for Person
The name every other table refers to the person by in the mock.
Job title as the roster writes it.
C to F. Drives the team cost, not the benefit rate.
Blank means unsquadded; net capacity only counts people on a squad.
Decides which bank holidays come off the person. Filtered to list = Region.
An Open vacancy brings zero net MW.
A lead takes the lead modifier rather than the default.
Semicolon separated, first entry is the primary skill. Alternative: an N:N to ListValue where skills need reporting on.
Workday Core ID. First thing an import matches on.
Workday File ID, matched alongside the Core ID.
Second thing an import matches on.
Matched with the IDs, not separately.
Empty means the Settings MW days (5). Scales working days, bank holidays and absence alike.
Overrides the default and lead modifiers for this person.
Date only, time zone independent.
Date only, time zone independent.
Links the person to the signed-in user, so "my work" filters and the Squad member role work.
The team the row belongs to.
A delivery squad. Capacity, utilisation and reservations are reported per squad.
Unique identifier for Squad
The person who leads it.
A palette name, not a literal colour. The app maps it onto a theme token.
The team the row belongs to.
A feature, spike or component. The register the whole plan hangs off.
Unique identifier for Work item
Unique, case insensitive. validate.ts refuses a duplicate.
Stored, but phaseOf() derives it from the state where the state names one.
How the item arrived. Front door for a promoted request, Direct for the new-work form, Jira for an import. Editable after creation.
A lookup, not a choice, because Settings lets the team edit the state model and its impacts.
Self-lookup. One level only, and the parent must be a Feature.
Filtered to list = Skill.
XS to XXL; the band carries the MW.
A typed total MW that replaces the band.
Stored as a choice because the forms read it as a word. commitment() still overrides it to Proposed when the state is Identified or In discovery.
The sprint number once the seed's quarter offset is applied. The engine reads span, never startSprint.
Stamped when the assessment is recorded.
Stamped when every benefit claim has an actual and the item is validated.
The key a Jira import matches on. Unique where present.
The primary benefit. Needs a landing month, a landing year and a business grade.
The grade whose rate values the released FTE.
At most one of Business grade and Grade blend is set. The mock keeps one text field, which is why validate.ts has to police name collisions between the two lists.
Required when the state's impact is Removed.
Required when the item is stopped. Cleared on Reopen.
Second self-lookup. Cannot be the item itself.
The close stamps it and reads it as its own guard against archiving twice.
Empty while the spike is still running.
The feature a feasible spike became. Third self-lookup.
The spike a feature came out of. Fourth self-lookup, kept because the mock stores both directions and the Close page reads them separately.
The team the row belongs to.
Unique identifier for Assignee
Work item title and person name, so the row reads in a grid.
A copy of the parent team, written by the app on create and on reparent so a filter never needs two hops.
Unique identifier for Assignment
Blank for a booking against no item, such as BAU.
Reservation category for non-work bookings; blank for work bookings, which carry a work item instead.
A copy of the parent team, written by the app on create and on reparent so a filter never needs two hops.
A person off, between two dates. Imported from Workday or typed on the Team page.
Unique identifier for Absence
Person name and dates, so the row reads in a lookup.
Filtered to list = Absence type. isSickness() treats anything starting "sick" as sickness.
Person, from and to, lower cased: the key the importer dedupes on.
A copy of the parent team, written by the app on create and on reparent so a filter never needs two hops.
Unique identifier for Benefit claim
FTE released is not valid here.
T to Y. Kept so a workbook round trip still lands in the right column.
Units vary by type: T is £M a year, U and V are percentages, W is a multiple.
A copy of the parent team, written by the app on create and on reparent so a filter never needs two hops.
What was really recorded against a claim, and the month it was recorded in.
Unique identifier for Benefit actual
FTE released and Cost avoidance are the two benefitValue() reads.
Blank for an FTE released actual, which has no claim row.
The mock's type allows a string and treats one as zero; Dataverse takes a number, and the form already refuses a blank.
The first of the month it landed in. The pro-rating reads month and year only.
A copy of the parent team, written by the app on create and on reparent so a filter never needs two hops.
Capacity held for a squad, or across the team, before the work is known.
Unique identifier for Reservation
Blank means Team: capacity held across every squad. The mock writes the word Team in the same field.
Explicit, so a blank squad is never mistaken for missing data.
Filtered to list = Reservation category. Discovery and Spikes draw on the same MW, so the form refuses both for one squad and quarter.
The team the row belongs to.
Unique identifier for Quarter
e.g. Q4 2026. quarterRange() parses it: Q, the number, then a four digit year.
The close moves to the next label on the list, so the order has to be explicit.
Written when the row is created; Dataverse cannot parse the label itself.
The Monday every sprint number counts from. 2026-01-05 in the seed.
14 in the seed.
53 in the seed. The grid starts at the ISO Monday on or before 1 January.
Exactly one row is true. The close moves the flag.
Written by the quarter close flow.
Blank means shared across the platform.
Unique identifier for Setting
Always "Waypoint".
0.3 in the seed.
0.4 in the seed.
The mock stores Yes or No as text; a Boolean says the same thing.
Must be above amber.
Must be above low confidence.
What one released FTE at that grade is worth a year.
Unique identifier for Business grade
A, B, C, D, Offshore and Contractor day rate in the seed. Cannot collide with a blend name.
Blank means shared across the platform.
A named mix of grades. Its rate is the weighted average of the grades in it.
Unique identifier for Grade blend
Ops mix in the seed, three C and ten D. Cannot collide with a grade name.
Blank means shared across the platform.
Unique identifier for Grade blend line
Unique identifier for Work state
Identified, In discovery, Ready, In development, Released, In validation, Done, Deferred, Cancelled.
The Jira Align wording this state maps from. Released reads 'Ready for release, Deployed, Live'.
Blank means shared across the platform.
A business outcome. Epics serve it; one epic serves one outcome.
Unique identifier for Outcome
Appended to the Jira Align base URL.
The team that owns it.
Unique identifier for Epic
Blank where no outcome claims the epic; outcomeOfEpic() returns an empty string for that case.
The team that owns it.
Unique identifier for Bank holiday
Filtered to list = Region.
Only counted when it falls Monday to Friday.
Unique identifier for Quarter snapshot
The team the row belongs to.
Unique identifier for Archive row
The category name on a Reservation row.
Work or Reservation. The mock leaves it blank for work.
For navigation only; the text columns stand alone if the item is later deleted.
The first assignee only, as the close writes it.
Done on time, Done late, Done, Cancelled, or Reserved on a reservation row.
Text, not a lookup, so recalibrating a band does not rewrite history.
Reservation rows only.
The team the row belongs to.
Unique identifier for Activity log
What was done, as the commit names it: e.g. Commit Statement matching rules v2.
What changed, in a phrase: e.g. 3 items committed, 1 deferred. A separate column from the label, as LogEntry keeps them.
Logical name of the table the change landed on.
The GUID as text, so the log survives the record.
User local behaviour; the log is read by people, not by the engine.
The changed columns as they were, one per line. Not a full record dump.
The quarter current at the time, so a close reads in context.
Unique identifier for Import profile
JSON: field key to header, null where the export has no such column. Read with ParseJSON.
JSON: field key to a map of export value onto model value, such as Jira status onto planner state.
iso, dmy or mdy. Detected per file; stored as a hint.
Unique identifier for Import run
File name and time.
One line per skipped row: No person matched, No worker name, No start date, Not approved, Already recorded, No issue key, No summary.
A copy of the parent team, written by the app on create and on reparent so a filter never needs two hops.
A t-shirt size and the member weeks it is worth. Calibration suggests changes to it.
Unique identifier for Size band
XS, S, M, L, XL, XXL.
0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8 and 13 in the seed.
Unique identifier for List value
For Role list values: the team grade this role maps to (C, D, E, F).
Blank means shared across the platform.
What one head at a team grade costs a year. Feeds cost of ownership on Money.
Unique identifier for Team grade cost
C, D, E or F. Text because a Dataverse primary column has to be text; the wp_teamgrade choice is the same list where a form wants a picker.
The team the row belongs to.
A licence, subscription or piece of infrastructure, and what it costs a year.
Unique identifier for Cost line
The team the row belongs to.
Unique identifier for Request
A short title for the request. Not unique.
The signed-in user who submitted it. Blank where the row was loaded rather than typed.
Pre-filled from the signed-in user, and kept as text so the request reads without the user row.
The person who will back it, and who knows they are being named.
Where the requester thinks it belongs. Blank is an answer.
Where the requester thinks it belongs. Blank is an answer, and the product owner sets it on screening.
Blue Prism, Power Automate, Power Apps, Copilot Studio or Other.
Only where the product line is Other.
One sentence. It becomes the spike question on promotion.
Roughly how many people feel the problem.
Step by step, as it runs today.
How many times it runs. The period is the frequency beside it.
How long one run takes a person. With the volume it is the time released estimate.
Semicolon separated where the requester lists them.

The same set the work item and the claims use, so the estimate carries across on promotion.
Free text, because a requester estimates in people or in pounds and a guess is fine.
What could stop this working. Policy, access, a contract, a team that has to agree.
A link rather than files. Real attachments are deferred.
New on submit. Only the product owner and the engineering lead move it on.
With the created date it is how long a request waited for a decision.
